title: Not all angels are in heaven…
summary: "Not all angels are in heaven… some are" plus your whole personality. AI helps you find a funny, true ending that fits your job or your quirks.
why: An Instagram Reels trends roundup updated October 23, 2026 lists "Not all angels are in heaven" as a trend from October 16: on-screen text starts the line, and creators finish it with something that fits their job or their quirks.
steps: Film a short clip of yourself doing the thing that makes you you: at your desk, in your kitchen, behind the counter.
Use the main prompt to get a list of endings, then pick the one that makes you laugh.
Add "Not all angels are in heaven…" as text first, then reveal the ending a second later.
Post with a trending sound from the app.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: Help me finish this on-screen text: "Not all angels are in heaven… some are". Give me 10 endings, each under 12 words. Make them about me, based on these details: my job is [your job], my funny habits are [two or three habits], and people always ask me for help with [one thing]. Keep it kind and a little self-mocking. No hashtags, no emojis.

prompts.label: Variation: the friend group
prompts.text: Give me 8 endings for "Not all angels are in heaven… some are" about a friend group role, like the one who always drives, the one who brings snacks or the one who remembers every birthday. I'm usually [your role]. Each ending under 12 words, warm and funny.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [your type of business]. Write 8 endings for "Not all angels are in heaven… some are" from the point of view of my business or my team. Think small, real things we do for customers, like [one or two examples]. Each ending under 12 words. Friendly, not salesy. Don't make up prices, reviews or deadlines.

tips: The more specific the ending, the better. "Answering emails at 11 p.m." beats "working hard".
Leave a short pause before the ending so people read the first part.
Keep the clip quiet and simple so the text does the work.
Only use friends in the video if they've said yes.
